Gabriel Weil — Overcoming Judgment-Proofness: The Law & Economics of Insuring and Mitigating AI Risk (SSRN, 2026) · a detailed summary, plus a critical Oggy Assessment

Gabriel Weil argues that tort liability cannot discipline catastrophic AI risk, because judgment-proofness severs the deterrent signal once losses exceed a firm's assets and insurance. He would require frontier developers to carry liability insurance scaled to the worst harms their systems could plausibly cause, making insurers delegated private regulators. For the uninsurable tail he operationalizes punitive damages for near misses: where an ordinary compensable harm is shown by clear and convincing evidence to have been a near miss of an uninsurable catastrophe, courts would award damages calibrated to the uninsurable risk the conduct created. The last three minutes are Oggy's own critical assessment, not the article's view.
